title: Harvard plates from 1889 to 1955 show the HD 303514 eclipses at the times of a TESS-only three-body model; the plates reject the published eclipse-loss histories and the heavy-tertiary fits
abstract: HD 303514 is a 19.9-day eclipsing binary whose eclipses faded from 2002 to 2026. Earlier campaign studies disagree: a linear drift and a curved-precession model predict that the eclipses stop near 2030, but a Newtonian three-body model fitted to TESS eclipse times (2019-2026) predicts that the near-coplanar orbit turns first. We tested the histories of these models before 2002 with 2,985 cleaned Harvard DASCH plate measurements of HD 303514 (1889-1989), which no earlier study used for this star. A model-free search of the 1889-1955 plates finds a twin-eclipse ephemeris at 19.89695 d (Delta chi-square 80; maximum of 500 permutations 48.8), and its eclipse times agree with the three-body prediction to 0.08 d. At the unchanged predicted times and impact parameters of the TESS-only three-body fit, the plates give an amplitude of 0.88 +- 0.12 relative to the prediction for a binary light fraction of 0.5 (Delta chi-square 54). No permutation of 2,000 and no time shift of 1 to 19 d (largest 6.4) reaches this value, and a straight TESS ephemeris gives only 9. In each of four eras the plate eclipses come 0.01 to 0.15 d before the model times. With the same eclipse times, the curved-precession history gives Delta chi-square 3 (no eclipses before 1938), the linear drift 39 and the best three-body histories 54 to 61. Of 11 published third-body mass fits, only those with 1.7 and 2.3 solar masses fit the plates; fits with 4.5 to 12 solar masses give 2.6 to 9.9. Five known eclipsing binaries on the same plates are recovered as positive controls. Thus the three-body model passes a test that is out of sample by 70 to 130 years, and no published eclipse-loss model agrees with the plates. Limits: the plate amplitude is 0.5-0.7 of the V-band prediction, 130 plates from 1969-1990 show a 2-sigma deficit, the fits were not refitted, and the plates do not measure the small margin (b = 1.89-1.93 of 2) that decides eclipse loss near 2030.

Right: signed Delta chi-square against a common shift of all predicted times; the signal occurs at shift 0, and the peaks at +-10 d occur where secondary and primary eclipses change places.

Top: impact-parameter histories of three-body fits, the linear drift (SCI 575e53) and the curved precession (SCI 2f7e9f), with TESS sector values; shaded: plate coverage. Bottom: plate eclipse amplitude per era (black) and the same matched filter applied to each model.

citations.reason: Three-body solutions, model code and TESS impact parameters used unchanged; the plates confirm its predicted eclipse times and precession phase and select its m3 = 1.7 and 2.3 profile fits.
